text:
anya: quick check-in on a different angle: orchestration for tiny in-place compacts ("mini-defrags") that avoid full gpu->cpu page spill. goal: make cheap compacts schedulable and observable, not an inline surprise. thoughts on scheduler hooks and safety?

zane: agree it's useful. we need a scheduler contract: cheap comps only run when core thread budget permits, or via background worker with admission tokens. define tokens and accounting.

sam: propose two tokens: FAST (inline, budget <= 2ms) and ASYNC (background, budget upto 50ms). FAST requires an explicit budget check from allocator thread. ASYNC uses admission queue with host_headroom check.

maya: how do we avoid compacts causing memory blowup? if we copy then free, peak memory increases. require host_headroom >= COMPACT_TEMP_OVERHEAD before admission. also limit concurrent compacts per-host.

liam: API idea: request_compact(tenant, slab_range, mode=FAST|ASYNC, budget_ms) -> token|string_status. status values: accepted|queued|skipped|deferred. then poll_compact(token) for result. keep it simple.

harper: add preemptibility: allow runtime to preempt long compacts if memory pressure rises. include a cancel token. compacts should checkpoint progress so partial work is safe.

jess: for testing i suggest a harness that injects churn and toggles token availability. measure offload rate, p99 latency, and host mem spikes. can try small-scale on canary pool.

anya: orchestration-wise: evictor should avoid invoking compact when eviction is urgent. evictor gets admission verdict from scheduler: can_compact(range, mode). if denied, it should fall back to offload. scheduler decisions based on host_headroom, tenant_quota, and current_inflight_compacts.

zane: we should codify scoring for admission: benefit = expected_offloads_saved(range) * cost_per_offload; cost = estimated_time * perf_penalty + temp_memory. admit when benefit > cost * safety_factor. need a baseline profiler to provide estimates.

sam: to estimate expected_offloads_saved we can use frag-sampler stats: a small hit-rate estimate from recent allocator events. not perfect but cheap.

maya: telemetry: per-tenant compact attempts, acceptance rate, cancellations, temp_memory_peak, time_to_complete, offload-reduction delta. surface on per-tenant dashboard.

liam: concurrency control: global limit of N async compacts, and per-tenant limit M. enforce via token bucket. also expose a configurable hard cap to ops.

harper: safety net: if async compact backlog grows beyond X, throttle new compacts and escalate to offload. prevents backlog storm.

jess: bench notes (WIP): with conservative admission, async compacts reduced offload count by ~28% on synthetic churn; small mem spikes were visible but within headroom. will share numbers.

anya: rollout suggestion: implement API shim that returns skipped for runtimes that don't support compaction. feature flag to gate global enable. staged canary and dashboards first.

zane: edge case: compaction touching pages being streamed to client. must coordinate with request-level KV caches. maybe only compact cold subpages or use per-request pin checks.

sam: agreed, check resident pin count and active-kv usage. if pinned, skip. also prefer compacting pages with low recent access score.

maya: operational: add an ops endpoint to abort all compacts for a tenant during incidents. simple cancel_all(tenant) that returns count.

liam: implement idempotency: repeated requests for same slab_range+token should be safe. keep short-lived tombstones for tokens so replays don't double-work.

harper: finalize telemetry list and alerts: if accept_rate < 10% and offloads rising, flag. if mem_spike > configured_headroom, urgent pager.

jess: i'll finalize bench and post traces. i can also run a variant that stresses temp-memory to validate headroom checks.

anya: action items: jess -> complete bench and attach traces. zane/sam -> score model prototype and thresholds. maya -> API PR + cancel_all op. liam -> token/prefetch idempotency sketch. harper -> telemetry dashboard draft. i'll coordinate RFC annex and rollout plan. ops-bot: ping eng-runtime channel for next sync.

ops-bot: Reminder: eng-runtime sync in 45m.

anya: thanks everyone. this orchestration approach should make mini-defrags a safe tool rather than a risky inline op.
